title: beta-Hydroxybutyrate Exacerbates Klebsiella pneumoniae-Induced Inflammatory Injury and Milk Synthesis Impairment via the GPR109A/NF-kappaB Signaling Axis.
authors: Wang, Jue; Yuan, Changning; Cai, Siyi; Ni, Luanyu; Liu, Kangjun; Guo, Long; Cui, Luying; Dong, Junsheng; Li, Jianji; Zhu, Guoqiang; Wang, Ran; Zhang, Lili; He, Tao; Meng, Xia; Wang, Heng
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
one_liner_zh: 该文研究BHBA通过GPR109A/NF-kappaB轴加重肺炎克雷伯菌诱导的乳腺炎，虽含分子对接但核心为炎症信号通路与代谢，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Ketotic cows exhibit a heightened mastitis risk through an unknown mechanism. This study investigated the influence of beta-hydroxybutyrate (BHBA) on mastitis development. Mammary tissues from ketotic cows with mastitis showed more severe pathological damage and suppression of lactation-related genes. BHBA pretreatment further increased NF-kappaB pathway activation, facilitated expressions of pro-inflammatory cytokines, and suppressed lactation proteins in Klebsiella pneumoniae (K. pneumoniae)-infected BMECs, thereby exacerbating inflammatory injury and milk synthesis impairment. Molecular docking, DARTS, and CETSA assays confirmed that BHBA directly bound to GPR109A. GPR109A knockdown blocked the activation of the NF-kappaB pathway, alleviated inflammatory injury, and mitigated milk synthesis impairment. Meanwhile, similar findings were identified with PTX (an inhibitor of GPR109A) treatment. These findings elucidated the role of BHBA and its endogenous receptor GPR109A in K. pneumoniae-induced inflammatory injury and milk synthesis impairment, which provided valuable insight for understanding the interplay between metabolic imbalance and postpartum mammary health.
abstract_zh: 酮症奶牛通过一种未知机制表现出更高的乳腺炎风险。本研究探讨了β-羟基丁酸（BHBA）对乳腺炎发展的影响。患有乳腺炎的酮症奶牛乳腺组织显示出更严重的病理损伤和泌乳相关基因的抑制。BHBA预处理进一步增强了NF-kappaB通路的激活，促进了促炎细胞因子的表达，并抑制了肺炎克雷伯菌（K. pneumoniae）感染的牛乳腺上皮细胞（BMECs）中的泌乳蛋白，从而加剧了炎症损伤和乳合成障碍。分子对接、DARTS和CETSA实验证实BHBA直接结合GPR109A。GPR109A敲低阻断了NF-kappaB通路的激活，减轻了炎症损伤，并缓解了乳合成障碍。同时，使用PTX（一种GPR109A抑制剂）处理也发现了类似的结果。这些发现阐明了BHBA及其内源性受体GPR109A在肺炎克雷伯菌诱导的炎症损伤和乳合成障碍中的作用，为理解代谢失衡与产后乳腺健康之间的相互作用提供了宝贵见解。
